articles.summary: A new character poster from 'Ramayana' has introduced Jatayu, the legendary bird known for his courage and sacrifice in the Indian epic.
articles.body: A new character poster from 'Ramayana' has introduced Jatayu, the legendary bird known for his courage and sacrifice in the Indian epic. The character will be voiced by veteran actor Anupam Kher, bringing another familiar name into the film’s ensemble. The poster offers a glimpse of Jatayu’s appearance, highlighting the character’s intense gaze and majestic form. His inclusion brings attention to one of the epic’s important moments, in which courage and duty take centre stage.Anupam Kher’s Jatayu poster highlights courage and dharmaThe newly released 'Ramayana' poster presents Jatayu in two striking visuals. One focuses on the bird’s face and sharp, determined eyes, while the other shows him with his wings spread wide. The reveal carries the title “The Wings of Dharma,” reflecting Jatayu’s role as a symbol of bravery and righteousness. Rather than relying only on his appearance, the character’s significance comes from his decision to stand against evil despite the danger. Anupam Kher’s voice will bring the character to life in the film.Why does Jatayu’s fight against Ravana matter?In the 'Ramayana,' Jatayu attempts to rescue Sita when Ravana abducts her. Although he knows that Ravana is a powerful opponent, the bird chooses to confront him rather than remain a silent witness. His attempt to stop the abduction ends in a tragic defeat, but his courage makes him an important figure in the epic. Jatayu’s actions represent sacrifice, loyalty, and the willingness to stand up for what is right, even when success seems unlikely. The character remains memorable because his bravery is defined by his choice to act, not by whether he wins the battle.Ranbir Kapoor and Sai Pallavi lead Nitesh Tiwari’s 'Ramayana'Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, 'Ramayana' features Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, Sunny Deol as Hanuman and Ravi Dubey as Lakshman. The film is planned as a two-part adaptation of the epic, with the first instalment scheduled for a worldwide theatrical release on November 5, 2026, and the second part planned for Diwali 2027.Produced by Namit Malhotra, the project brings together performers from different film industries to tell the well-known story for a new generation. Having effortlessly crossed major domestic milestones during its extended first week, the investigative thriller is demonstrating remarkable staying power during weekdays. With Day 12 in cinemas, all eyes are on whether it can swiftly cross the elusive Rs. 500 crore global threshold before the next wave of major releases like Rajkummar Rao led 'Prahaar' and Yami Gautam starrer 'Nayyi Navelli' hits screens.'Drishyam 3 The Conclusion' domestic box office runThe film earned Rs. 245.50 crore net in week 1 and Rs. 294.60 crore gross. The India net crossed Rs. 309 crore, with a gross of Rs 370.80 crore. Day 11 added Rs. 6.25 crore, a typical Monday drop, and lifted the India net to Rs.315.25 crore.‘Drishyam 3 The Conclusion’ overseas collection and worldwide totalOverseas, the film made Rs. 89 crore in week 1, with a strong start of Rs. 18.50 crore on Day 1, Rs. 23 crore on Day 2 and Rs 21 crore on Day 3. Day 8 added Rs. 6 crore, Day 9 brought Rs. 8 crore, and Day 10 contributed Rs 6 crore. Day 11 added Rs. 2.50 crore, which takes the overseas gross to Rs. 111.50 crore. Directed by Abhishek Pathak, Ajay Devgn reprises his iconic role as Vijay Salgaonkar, the resourceful family man who relies on cinema-inspired logic and strategic foresight to shield his family from law enforcement. The ensemble cast features Tabu returning as former IG Meera Deshmukh alongside Rajat Kapoor as Mahesh Deshmukh. articles.body: Cada vez son más los personajes públicos que deciden opinar sobre política en público y en redes sociales. Por eso, sorprende que, algunos de los que no lo han hecho, comiencen a pronunciarse sin problema y a debatir como cualquier otro ciudadano. El último ha sido C. Tangana. El cantante ha entrado en el debate sobre la unidad de la izquierda a raíz del acuerdo entre ERC y Podemos para las generales del 29 de noviembre. El madrileño ha reaccionado en Instagram a un vídeo de ‘Malas Lenguas’ en el que Pablo Iglesias analizaba el pacto, con un duro reproche a los personalismos. En su mensaje, el músico fue tajante y salió en defensa de Rufián ante las críticas por presentarse por su partido: “Rufián no iba a ganarle votos a un partido, iba a intentar parar un gobierno de Vox. Y lo que no tiene sentido es priorizar las carreras personales y los éxitos particulares cuando la gente está pidiendo cosas muy claras. Puro ego”. En el programa, Iglesias defendió que Rufián ha sido leal a su partido y recordó sus palabras: “Soy de Esquerra Republicana y no me cambio de partido”. Aún así, subrayó que ha favorecido “un acuerdo histórico”, algo que “no ocurre muchas veces”. También destacó que ha empujado a ERC hacia un mayor encuentro con otras fuerzas progresistas. Días antes, Iglesias ya había anticipado en el mismo programa de RTVE este paso de ambas fuerzas políticas: “Yo creo que Rufián no se va a ir de su partido. Habrá algún tipo de encuentro para que forme parte de algo”. Sobre Más Madrid, Iglesias evitó entrar en rencillas sobre quién debe encabezar las listas, al tratarse de un partido de ámbito regional, y defendió que en Madrid puede haber diferentes candidaturas. Lo fundamental es que en el resto del país se alcancen acuerdos con formaciones como Compromís, Chunta Aragonesista, Més o Nueva Canarias para construir “una candidatura ilusionante” con Rufián e Irene Montero al frente. Iglesias también desea un acuerdo con Ada Colau, ya que en una circunscripción como Barcelona “cualquier voto cuenta”. Reclamó candidaturas fuertes que pongan la vivienda en el centro para hacer frente a la derecha. Un llamamiento a sumar que enlaza con la crítica de C. Tangana.

articles.title: Selma Blair, detenida por intentar abrir la puerta de un avión, pegar y morder a la tripulación
articles.standfirst: La intérprete de ‘Una rubia muy legal’ pudo sufrir una emergencia médica
articles.summary: La intérprete de ‘Una rubia muy legal’ pudo sufrir una emergencia médica
articles.body: La Autoridad Portuaria de Nueva York y el Departamento de Policía de Nueva Jersey han informado de la detención de Selma Blair, actriz conocida por sus papeles en ‘Una rubia muy legal’ y ‘Crueles intenciones’, entre otras. Al parecer, la intérprete de 51 años intentó abrir una de las puertas del avión en el que viajaba de Los Ángeles a Nueva York, además de morder y pegar a dos tripulantes. Según explica el portal TMZ, Blair estaba a bordo de un avión de la compañía Delta cuando se desarrollaron los hechos. Tras ser increpada por intentar abrir la puerta, golpeó directamente a un auxiliar y se lanzó a morder a otro cuando trataban de impedir que lograra su objetivo en pleno vuelo. Nada más aterrizar, los agentes de policía la esperaban en la puerta de embarque, donde fue detenida de inmediato y trasladada al hospital para una evaluación médica sobre su estado. Junto con ella, los dos auxiliares también tuvieron que ser atendidas como consecuencia de los incidentes a bordo. Un representante de la actriz, en declaraciones a Variety, ha querido explicar lo ocurrido y dar su versión: “Sufrió una emergencia médica que derivó en la conducta mencionada. Tras el aterrizaje, recibió atención médica inmediata y actualmente se encuentra estable”. Por su parte, la aerolínea ha emitido un comunicado y ha dejado claro que tiene “tolerancia cero” ante comportamientos como el de Selma Blair, que considera que son “conflictivos o ilegales”. “La seguridad de nuestros clientes y de la tripulación es siempre la prioridad”, añaden desde Delta Air Lines. A pesar de lo ocurrido, eso sí, el vuelo pudo completar su ruta sin mayores complicaciones y todos los pasajeros llegaron a su destino en el aeropuerto John F. Kennedy alrededor de las 23:00 horas.

articles.title: Raye hits back at ticket touts who took over Albert Hall sign-up
articles.summary: The award-winning singer said there were 1.8 million sign-ups for her 5,000-seat Royal Albert Hall show.
articles.body:
Raye has hit back at ticket touts who she says "overwhelmed" the sign-up process for an upcoming live show by using artificial intelligence (AI) bots to create "hundreds of thousands of fake registrations".

The Where Is My Husband! singer revealed there were 1.8 million sign-ups for her one-off 5,000-seat performance at the Royal Albert Hall on 23 October.

To avoid a pre-sale which she felt scalpers could exploit, Raye said the sign-up list had been manually reviewed to identify a shortlist of people believed to be "real fans".

A spokesperson for the Royal Albert Hall said they "invest heavily" in protecting their ticketing systems from "automated attacks" but the "law needs to catch up".

The award-winning artist said she had "never witnessed bots on this scale" and was changing the process as it is "so important" to her that fans can buy tickets at the face value price.

"I'm not sure what the future holds for ticketing, I do know this experience has really opened my eyes," she said in a statement shared on her social media accounts .

"Me and my team are going to think really hard about what we can do in the future."

Raye said the fans manually selected would receive a pre-sale link and code by email at 11:45 BST on Tuesday, and pre-sale opened shortly afterwards.

She added that the remaining tickets would be available to all on general sale.

This Symphony May Contain Hope show will showcase songs from her recent chart-topping second album, This Music May Contain Hope, that fuses old-school jazz with orchestral sound, blues, big band and soul.

The 17-track record is a concept album which explores overcoming heartbreak, self-doubt and internet trolling.

Raye has enjoyed an impressive past few years since leaving her label after expressing frustration that they were holding out on releasing her debut album.

She was later released from her contract and struck out as an independent artist.

By the end of 2022, her dance track Escapism featuring US rapper 070 Shake had gone viral on TikTok and shot up the charts to number one.

She finally released her emotionally-charged debut album, My 21st Century Blues, in 2023, which was applauded by critics and peaked at number two in the charts.

It went to on to win a record-breaking six Brit Awards , including album of the year, and was nominated for the acclaimed Mercury Prize.

This summer, Raye was among the six British and Irish artists who headlined Reading and Leeds Festival.

In November, dozens of musicians including Dua Lipa, Coldplay and Sam Fender called on the government to protect fans from online ticket touts in an open letter.

The government then announced plans to ban the resale of tickets for live events above face value.

A draft Ticket Tout Bill was put forward in May, but music industry and consumer groups voiced their frustration that more progress wasn't being made.

It will now go through further consultation and scrutiny, before it can become a new law.

Following Raye's statement, a spokesperson for the Department for Culture, Media and Sport said it remained "fully committed to stamping out ticket touting for good".

The Royal Albert Hall spokesperson said they "strongly support" the government's plan to improve ticketing laws.

"Artists and venues are doing everything they can to protect fans, but we cannot solve this problem alone," they added.

"The law needs to catch up with the scale and sophistication of the ticket touting industry."

articles.title: Ferran Adrià desvela lo que cobraba por ser copropietario del restaurante elBulli
articles.standfirst: Una cifra muy alejada de lo que muchos podrían imaginar al tratarse del restaurante más admirado del planeta en su momento
articles.summary: Una cifra muy alejada de lo que muchos podrían imaginar al tratarse del restaurante más admirado del planeta en su momento
articles.body: A Ferran Adriá se le asocia con el fenómeno de elBulli, el local que regentaba y que saltó a la fama bajo su codirección. Pero el tiempo pasa. Aquella empresa tocó a su fin. Y hoy solo queda el recuerdo. El establecimiento ya no recibe comensales al cerrar en 2011, si bien su legado sigue vivo a través de elBulliFoundation y del espacio museístico situado en la Costa Brava. Además, Adrià continúa compartiendo reflexiones sobre una etapa que cambió para siempre la alta cocina. Una de las más llamativas es cuando el chef catalán sorprendió al desvelar, en una entrevista a Ara, cuál era el sueldo que percibía como propietario de elBulli. Y llama la atención. Porque se trataba de una cifra muy alejada de lo que muchos podrían imaginar por tratarse del restaurante más admirado del planeta. "Durante muchos años gané lo que hoy equivaldría a 2.000 euros al mes. Era nuestro salario como propietarios de elBulli", señalaba Adriá. Y detallaba que el restaurante no era su principal fuente de ingresos ya que el modelo de negocio era especialmente complejo. De hecho, aseguró que llegó a compaginar su trabajo con labores de asesoramiento para una decena de multinacionales al mismo tiempo. No todo fue de dulce. Porque recordaba también que cuando llegó al restaurante en 1984 y hasta finales de los años noventa, la situación financiera fue compleja. "Como vale mucho dinero, la gente cree que ganamos mucho dinero. Esto no es así. Del 84 al 98 no ganábamos ni un duro. Había muchas veces que no podíamos pagar ni al personal porque no teníamos dinero". Por tanto, elBulli pese a ser tan reconocido y un lugar de culto culinario durante tanto tiempo, también tuvo que superar años de sacrificios, incertidumbre y cuentas al límite antes de convertirse en una leyenda.

articles.title: Kelly Clarkson's store callout shows the 'power' of celebrity statements: expert
articles.summary: Kelly Clarkson's viral feud with Brooklyn store Art of Play over a singing bird automaton has PR experts weighing the risks and opportunities.
articles.body: Kelly Clarkson's recent headline-making feud has public relations experts saying the viral attention brings risks for the store, but could create an opportunity if it handles the backlash well. Over the weekend, Clarkson called out Art of Play, a Brooklyn store known for its collection of toys, games, books, puzzles and other unique items, for allegedly denying her the ability to buy "Molly," a one-of-a-kind singing and dancing bird automaton. "Just drove all the way to Brooklyn to check out this store I thought looked really rad and had a few things in mind to buy and literally was looked at as if I couldn’t afford it and was told he could find something comparable for me," Clarkson wrote. "Wow, dude. You’re an idiot and just lost a huge sale," she continued. KELLY CLARKSON SLAMS BROOKLYN STORE OVER ‘PRETTY WOMAN’ TREATMENT Clarkson then compared the encounter to a memorable scene from the 1990 movie "Pretty Woman," in which Julia Roberts’ character, Vivian Ward, is dismissed by a boutique saleswoman who assumes she cannot afford the store’s clothing. "But y’all should go check out Art of Play in Brooklyn if you enjoy being treated like Julia Roberts’ character in ‘Pretty Woman.’ For sure, check it out," Clarkson added. The singer’s description of the incident echoed the famous "Pretty Woman" scene, in which Vivian returns to the boutique after being rejected and tells the saleswoman, "Big mistake. Big. Huge." A source told People: "She’s usually very private and public drama like this isn’t her." "She’s clearly so ticked off that she couldn’t keep quiet about it. Everyone is surprised by how much this whole thing has escalated," the insider told the outlet. Doug Eldridge, founder of Achilles PR, told Fox News Digital that this debacle speaks to three key points: "1. The power and presumptive veracity of celebrity statements and/or accusations; 2. The staggering pace and scale of social media as a tool of dissemination; 3. The critical need for a crisis communications plan, regardless of the size of your business." Art of Play posted a response to Clarkson's original social media callout, claiming that they have had "8 million people" bombarding them with hateful messages after the singer's accusations. "Imagine our surprise when our small local business was suddenly attacked by 8 million people who have never visited our store. It’s been a surreal experience to be the focus of such widespread outrage after just one mention by a celebrity. Thanks to all our friends for their support and welcome to all the curious folks who discovered us amidst the drama. We’re going to keep our heads down and hopefully, we can clear things up with Kelly someday. As a talented popular singer once said ‘what doesn’t kill you makes you stronger,’" the store posted to their Instagram page on Sunday afternoon. Eldridge continued, "Irrespective of which side you believe, this has proven Winston Churchill’s famous quip: 'A lie gets halfway around the world before the truth gets its pants on in the morning.'" After the store's Instagram post, Clarkson took to her X account and Instagram stories on Sunday afternoon to respond to their claims. "Cool, cool. Sure, it wasn't for sale. That's the narrative Art of Play is gonna go with," Clarkson wrote, adding a thumbs up emoji. The singer continued: "So the whole conversation we had when I asked you if it was for sale whilst pointing to the price tag hanging on the wall with the title Singing Bird didn't happen as you elevator eyed me saying in a condescending tone "yes, it’s for sale but it costs 15,000 dollars so if you’d like me to find something comparable for you I can." That all never happened and now it’s not for sale. Okay, cool. So you’re not only rude, you’re also a liar. Got it," adding a checkmark emoji. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS Clarkson added: "And by the way, I obviously support small businesses because I was literally at a small business trying to purchase things. I love small businesses and know they are important and I always support them, but you don’t get a free pass to treat people less than in your store just because you are a small business. It’s not that hard to be kind. I never blast people but you my friend were an exception. Your store is really cool. Unfortunately, you aren’t." Jay Aldebert, chief growth officer at International Services Inc. and creator of the Profit by Design Methodology, told Fox News Digital that there are two ways Art of Play could view Clarkson bringing millions of people's attention to their small business. WATCH: Kelly Clarkson’s social media callout could have 'devastating effect,' expert says "I think it can have two effects, right? The first effect is that you've seen people take up the banner in her name, and you see people posting bad reviews or, obviously, there's a lot of comments. So, there is a negativity that can have an effect. She's got a lot of social power. She has 40 million followers and her taking to social media and making a comment, I think you can have a devastating effect," he began. "But, if I were to make a counter, the counter is that all good press or all good heat or negative or positive heat, I guess is good and what the store does it with it right now I think can be quite eventful for them," Aldebert continued. Aldebert, who manages 1,000 people at his own firm, believes Clarkson should have taken her concerns about her treatment at the store to Art of Play's owner before blasting the whole business on social media. "If I'm Monday morning quarterback on this particular one, I'm going to say the first step you take is reach out to the owner, see if it can be resolved. If, obviously, it's treated as something where they just blow it off or they're rude, too, then I can kind of see, at least you wait out. You have a great weapon, which is your social media presence. And then take that step if necessary. But I would have liked to see that step taken in terms of the contact of the owner," he said. "It could be as simple and again, I'm just you know kind of taking a couple guesses in terms of what I would do in this, but photos with the bird. Why not charge five dollars to do so? You know, make a bunch of T-shirts as it relates to the products that resemble it," he began. GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE "Let's put those up front. If it's this bird out there then now people are going to want to see because, 'Hey, they wouldn't sell it to Kelly Clarkson. Will they sell it me?' I would increase the price. There's a lot of different aspects that they could be using this to generate more revenue," Aldebert said. "And I hope that they take action and maybe they get more of those birds. They're kind of gonna be like a prized possession for a short period of time." On Sunday, Art of Play took to social media to "clarify one additional detail" about Clarkson's visit. "During the 5 minutes she spent in the store, she inquired about our mechanical bird puppet named Molly. We explained that while Molly is permanently attached to the wall and serves as a de facto mascot for our shop, a nearly identical automaton is owned by the creator of the machines, a brilliant artist named Bliss Kolb who lives in Seattle. He told us he would be willing to part with Molly’s twin for $15,000. We explained all of this to Kelly Clarkson." articles.title: Metallica frontman James Hetfield blasts entertainers pushing political agendas at concerts
articles.summary: Metallica frontman James Hetfield took aim at concert politics amid Macklemore's removal from Ed Sheeran's tour over "Free Palestine" calls.
articles.body: Metallica frontman James Hetfield is calling out performers who bring political agendas to the stage. During Metallica's show at the Las Vegas Sphere on Saturday night, the 63-year-old musician took a moment to express his gratitude to fans who traveled to see the heavy metal band and blasted entertainers who turn concerts into political platforms. "Unless you live in Vegas, you've come a long way to spend some time with Metallica," he said in a video shared on YouTube. "We're grateful for that — your travels, the money you spend, the time it took, thanks for coming to celebrate with us." GOO GOO DOLLS' JOHN RZEZNIK DRAWS LINE ON POLITICS AT CONCERTS: 'I'M NOT GOING TO LECTURE YOU' "I just gotta say, Metallica is not here, like some other entertainers, to influence you with their bulls---, OK?," Hetfield continued as the audience clapped and cheered. "We are here … no bulls--- … we're here to forget about all the outside s---, OK?" he added. "Metallica's agenda is love, energy and heavy music, baby!" ED SHEERAN CONCERTGOERS WARN ARTISTS ABOUT SHARING POLITICAL VIEWS: 'YOU'RE GOING TO ALIENATE' FANS Although Hetfield did not name any artists, several musicians have recently made political statements during their concerts. Last month, Macklemore was dropped from his remaining scheduled performances on Ed Sheeran's "Loop Tour" after the rapper repeatedly called for a "Free Palestine" and performed his pro-Palestinian protest song "Hind's Hall" while opening for the "Shape of You" singer at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. MACKLEMORE'S LONG HISTORY OF CONTROVERSY FROM GRAMMY WINS TO 'FREE PALESTINE' CONCERT REMARKS At the time, Macklemore said Robert Kraft, owner of the New England Patriots and Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts, told Sheeran that the "Thrift Shop" hitmaker "would not be allowed" to perform at the stadium. Kraft later confirmed that he opposed Macklemore performing at Gillette Stadium, citing the rapper's "recent actions" and what he called a "broader history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery." ED SHEERAN APOLOGIZES FOR MACKLEMORE BACKLASH, ENCOURAGES UNITY AT FIRST CONCERT SINCE FALLOUT Following Macklemore's removal, all of Sheeran's remaining opening acts and supporting musicians, including Finneas, Lukas Graham, Aaron Rowe and Beoga, pulled out in solidarity with the rapper. In an Instagram statement, Sheeran said he was not responsible for Macklemore's removal, explaining that the promoter and venues made the decision. READ IT: ED SHEERAN'S PRE-CONCERT SPEECH TO PHILLY CROWD ABOUT THE GAZA CONTROVERSY During his show in Philadelphia, Sheeran said he was "appalled by the conflict between Israel and Palestine" and called the situation in Gaza "catastrophic and unjustifiable," while describing the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas-led attacks on Israel as "horrific." Sheeran has also defended his decision to keep his concerts apolitical. The four-time Grammy winner said his audience includes children and fans from a wide range of backgrounds who "do not expect a political forum" when they attend his shows. MACKLEMORE SLAMMED AS 'PERFORMATIVE' AFTER ANNOUNCING 'FREE PALESTINE TOUR' Macklemore subsequently pledged to donate the $1 million he earned opening for Sheeran to organizations providing humanitarian aid to Palestinians. He also announced a three-date "Free Palestine Tour" scheduled for late October. During the controversy, country singer Zach Bryan wore a "Free Palestine" T-shirt during his sold-out concerts at Gillette Stadium in October. SPRINGSTEEN, OTHER STARS SHARE STAGE WITH HARDCORE LEFTIST GROUPS AT MUSIC FEST Other musicians who have made political statements during concerts include Bruce Springsteen, Rage Against the Machine's Tom Morello, Green Day's Billie Joe Armstrong and Kacey Musgraves. Meanwhile, Hetfield has long expressed his opposition to mixing music and politics. In a 2016 interview with the BBC, he explained that Metallica steered clear of divisive topics. MICK JAGGER DOESN'T WANT TO 'LECTURE' FANS, SAYS HIS JOB IS TO MAKE PEOPLE 'HAVE THE BEST TIME' "There's a lot of polarization going on in the States, and I see it in other places as well," he said. "But it just seems like you have to get more extreme to balance out the other extreme. We've got to find some balance in the middle here somewhere." "We stay away from politics [and] from religion," Hetfield added. "That just seems to polarize people even more. We all have our own beliefs, but at the end of the day, we're trying to connect with people, and it seems like political views don't do that as much as music does." In a 2017 interview with the Chilean newspaper La Tercera, Hetfield declined to share his opinion of Donald Trump, who was president at the time, and reiterated his opposition to mixing music and politics. "I'm a singer and guitar player in a rock band," Hetfield continued. "I hate politics," he added. "I don't want to talk about politics. That separates people, and I want to connect them with music. I prefer to stay out of all that, because it polarizes people, because if I say 'I love Trump' or 'I hate Trump,' someone can say 'then I don't like his music anymore,' which is very silly." articles.title: Who is Kennedy Suarez, RJ Mitte’s fiancée? Inside their 10-year-long friendship, five-year romance and heartfelt engagement
articles.summary: RJ Mitte, the actor best known for playing Walter White Jr. on 'Breaking Bad,' passed away on Monday, October 12, 2026, at the age of 34.
articles.body: RJ Mitte, the actor best known for playing Walter White Jr. on 'Breaking Bad,' passed away on Monday, October 12, 2026, at the age of 34. He was found dead at his home in Brownsville, Texas. Mitte lived with cerebral palsy and turned that personal experience into a long public push for better representation of people with disabilities. His representatives confirmed the news, describing him as a beloved actor, philanthropist, and passionate disability rights advocate, as TMZ reported.Behind the headlines about his career and advocacy sat a quieter part of his life: his relationship with Kennedy Suarez, the woman he had planned to marry. The two got engaged on October 10, 2025, on her 30th birthday, in California. Suarez, who kept a low public profile, suddenly found herself at the centre of the story as people looked for more details about the partner Mitte had called his “everything.”RJ Mitte and Kennedy Suarez’s growing friendship that turned into a life togetherKennedy Suarez and RJ Mitte were friends for more than a decade before anything romantic started. The shift happened during a trip they took together, when both realised their feelings had grown past friendship. By the time they got engaged, they had been a couple for about five years and were living together in Brownsville. According to People, Suarez worked remotely as a human resources generalist, a job that let her travel with Mitte for film shoots and appearances.RJ Mitte’s proposal that marked Kennedy Suarez’s 30th birthdayMitte proposed to Suarez at the 56th annual Día del Sol fundraising gala in Carlsbad, California. The event supported United Cerebral Palsy of San Diego, an organisation for which Mitte served as an ambassador. He got down on one knee in front of the crowd, and she said yes. Afterwards, he told the outlet, “I’m thrilled to have found my person, my partner in life who makes me want to be better, no matter what we’re doing. Kennedy is my everything, and I can’t wait to officially start our life together and see what adventures life takes us on next.” The timing made the loss even sharper: he passed away just two days after the first anniversary of that proposal, and only days after she turned 31.Kennedy Suarez’s quiet role in his public workSuarez was not a public figure and did not have a high-profile career in entertainment. She supported his advocacy work, including efforts tied to the Mitte Foundation, which focused on community needs in South Texas, and she accompanied him to events connected to United Cerebral Palsy and disability rights. After getting engaged, Suarez, Mitte dearly wrote on Instagram, “I’ve found that love is not always sunshine and rainbows, and for me, what love comes down to is trust and believing in each other, regardless of the situation, during the good times, the bad times, and everything in between! I’ve been grateful for all the love and kindness I have been given over the years, but Kennedy has been the greatest unconditional love no matter what we are going through, no matter what we are facing type love and we face it all together. I will never stop lifting her like she has for me and can’t wait for our future.”What remains of the future they talked aboutIn the year after the engagement, the couple did not rush into wedding planning. Mitte continued acting and promoting projects, including the film Talking to Strangers, and kept posting occasional tributes to Suarez. On Valentine’s Day 2026, he shared photos of them with the caption: “Happy Valentine’s Day. Looking back at these moments with you reminds me how grateful I am for the love and kindness we share. Love transcends all. Go out and share yours.” Those words now sit alongside the earlier ones about wanting to start their life together. At 31, Suarez is left to navigate the sudden end of a relationship that began as a long friendship and grew into an engagement built on shared days, travel, and mutual support. Mitte’s death has drawn attention to the private person he chose, even as the details of her life remain limited by her own preference for staying out of the public eye.The story of Kennedy Suarez is still unfolding in the quietest way possible. While tributes pour in for Mitte’s work on screen and his advocacy off it, the woman he planned to marry has stepped back, consistent with the private life she maintained even when she stood beside him at galas and premieres. What is clear from the public record is that for several years she was the constant presence in the part of his life that cameras rarely captured.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: In 1967, Marlon Brando acquired a Polynesian atoll; his vision for the island lives on through conservation efforts
articles.summary: Marlon Brando stood among the defining actors of the twentieth century, a performer whose intensity and naturalism reshaped American film.
articles.body: Marlon Brando stood among the defining actors of the twentieth century, a performer whose intensity and naturalism reshaped American film. Roles in A Streetcar Named Desire, On the Waterfront and later The Godfather made him a global figure, yet the glare of that fame often left him restless. He looked for places where the noise of Hollywood could not follow, and he found one during the filming of Mutiny on the Bounty. The quiet ring of islets known as Tetiaroa offered the distance and beauty he craved, turning a personal escape into a lasting vision for protection and careful living that still guides the atoll today.The clear lagoon, the small coral islets known as motus, and the simple beauty of the place—it all stayed with him. A few years later, in 1966, he secured the rights to the atoll, a roughly 1,445-acre ring of twelve islets about thirty miles north of Tahiti.What began as a personal escape from Hollywood fame turned into something bigger: a lifelong wish to keep the place wild, to study it, and to show that people could live lightly on the land. Decades after his death in 2004, that wish is still unfolding through careful conservation work, scientific research, and a low-impact resort that carries his name.A personal refuge that grew into lasting protectionBrando first saw Tetiaroa during location scouting and was struck by its isolation and the shifting blues of the lagoon. “For Marlon, Tetiaroa was his paradise,” said Mike Medavoy, who was the actor’s friend and co-executor of his estate, in an interview with The Hollywood Reporter.As reported by Yahoo Travel, after marrying his Tahitian co-star Tarita Teriipaia and starting a family, he negotiated a long-term arrangement for the atoll, often described as a 99-year lease rather than outright ownership in the usual sense and treated it as a private haven.Marlon did not want heavy development. The decision to keep most of the atoll untouched was a broader part of his plan. He wanted Tetiaroa to become an ecologically responsible tropical resort, a nature preserve, an open-air experimental science laboratory—a “university of the sea,” as reported by the Los Angeles Times. It created the foundation for everything that followed, giving wildlife and the natural shoreline room to recover instead of being pushed aside.A vision for science and learning on the waterBrando imagined scientists and students coming together to study the lagoon, the reefs, and Polynesian culture, while testing practical ideas for living more gently, such as solar power, waste handling, and ways to protect fragile island ecosystems.Marlon subscribed to science magazines and technical journals. He vividly studied Tetiaroa's water tables, the quality of the soil, and the flora and fauna of the region. In the early days, he applied himself hands-on to Tetiaroa’s plumbing challenges.In his later years, any plumber called to the Mulholland Drive house would find himself followed around by Marlon, who’d also peer underneath the sinks alongside him and ask about torque wrench brands and hose bib fits.Showing that careful tourism can support natureBrando hoped the atoll could welcome visitors without spoiling what made it special. He wanted an ecological model where tourism, conservation, and local culture worked together. That idea took shape after his death. His estate worked with Pacific Beachcomber to open The Brando in 2014, a 35-villa eco-friendly resort that doubles as a nature preserve.It was a small luxury resort that opened in 2014 on one motu. Buildings sit back among the trees so lights do not disturb nesting turtles. The resort uses seawater air-conditioning, solar power, and careful waste systems, and a large share of its support goes to the Tetiaroa Society’s work.Guests can learn about the island’s history and ecology while the rest of the atoll stays largely undisturbed, proving that limited, thoughtful access can fund protection rather than threaten it.Wildlife recovery that keeps the original promiseThe clearest sign that Brando’s vision continues is the return of the animals. Teams from the Tetiaroa Society and research partners such as Te mana o te moana monitor green sea turtles every season. Teams recorded more than 15,600 hatchlings emerging from roughly 161 nests in a single season, according to Upworthy.According to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), the green sea turtle, known as honu in Tahitian, is the world’s largest hard-shelled sea turtle, which is central to that vision. The atoll is one of the region’s major nesting sites for the endangered species, and protecting the turtles is a core activity of the atoll’s on-site Ecostation research hub.Today Tetiaroa remains private and carefully managed. The combination of research, limited tourism, and hands-on protection means Brando’s early hope—that the atoll could serve the planet as well as the people who visit or study it—has not faded. It lives on in the turtles crossing the sand, the scientists at the eco-station, and the quiet decision to leave most of the motus wild.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: 'Don't think PM Narendra Modi is so weak that his government would call me up for such a small show,' says Shekhar Suman as he defends comments made on his show
articles.summary: Actor and television host Shekhar Suman has addressed speculation surrounding his YouTube satire show ‘Shekhar Tonite’, saying it is a misconception that
articles.body: Actor and television host Shekhar Suman has addressed speculation surrounding his YouTube satire show ‘Shekhar Tonite’, saying it is a misconception that the programme targets the BJP-led government at the Centre. In an interview recently, he maintained that his commentary is directed at shortcomings in the system rather than any particular political party. He also said he does not believe Prime Minister Narendra Modi or his government would feel threatened by the show.Suman explained that his approach to political satire has remained consistent over the years, irrespective of which party is in power. Comparing the government to a class monitor, he said in an interview with The Lallantop, “If the class monitor lapses, the students would panic and hold him accountable, right? It doesn’t matter who the monitor is,” stressing that those in positions of authority must be held accountable for their actions.He cited his earlier television show ‘Movers & Shakers’, which first aired in 1997 when the BJP was in power at the Centre and returned in 2012 under the Congress-led government, as an example of his longstanding approach to satire.Emphasising that his comedy has never been about targeting a particular leader or party, Suman said, “Like we used to take digs at PM Atal Bihari Vajpayee earlier, we’d take digs at PM Manmohan Singh. We don’t comment on any person or any government, but on the system at large. If you’ve elected someone to lead the system, if they go astray, you point it out to them. That’s why it’s not anti-anyone, but pro-people. We’re just representing people and amplifying their voice. We’ll do that tomorrow as well when someone else would be in power,” he said.Suman added that he holds both Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Congress leader and Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi in high regard, but believes that criticism is justified when something goes wrong. “But when something wrong happens, it becomes legitimate to speak against that,” he said.Addressing concerns about social media videos critical of Modi allegedly being taken down, Suman acknowledged that such instances do occur but argued that the larger issue lies with the system. “It happens. It is happening. You can’t hold any person accountable for this, but the system is going wrong somewhere. Those who are leading are just faces. But there should be accountability.”The actor also denied receiving any calls from the BJP-led government asking him to tone down his commentary or discontinue the show. Instead, he claimed that several politicians had contacted him to express their appreciation for the programme.“I don’t think PM Modi is so weak that his government would call me up for such a small show. He’s a very powerful being. There are a lot of other things happening around the globe which warrant his attention far more. There are other sorrows in the world besides Shekhar Tonite,” he said, invoking a line from Faiz Ahmad Faiz’s poem ‘Mujhse Pehli Si Mohabbat Mere Mehboob Na Maang’.Suman recalled that when the first episode of ‘Shekhar Tonite’ premiered on YouTube, many viewers predicted that a second episode would never see the light of day. He questioned why anyone would assume the show would be stopped, pointing out that Modi himself had spoken about welcoming criticism.“Why? Who’d stop it? PM Modi? He himself has said it multiple times that he likes to be critiqued. So, we took a cue from there. I’m presuming he has a sense of humour, and he wouldn’t take it so seriously. It’s part of democracy, and part of my profession. What we’re saying is in the framework of entertainment and satire. So, there’s no reason for the government to get worried. My show isn’t that important,” he said.He further revealed that his initial reaction to receiving calls from BJP politicians was one of apprehension, as he wondered whether the conversations might involve complaints about the show. However, he said the interactions turned out to be positive, with some politicians even visiting his home.“But that wasn’t the case. Some politicians even visited my home. They’re all honest and sincere people. A lot of people spread this misinformation that it’s an environment of fear, and no one can say anything against anyone. Why can’t they? People are raising their voice,” he said.Through his remarks, Suman reiterated that he views satire as a way to question those in power and represent public concerns, rather than as an attack on any individual or political party.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: In 2017, Kevin Hart established Help from the Hart; a year later, he partnered with the United Negro College Fund and KIPP public schools to create a $600,000 scholarship program
articles.summary: Kevin Hart is the kind of individual who makes you laugh until your sides hurt, then turns around and uses that same energy to lift people.
articles.body: Kevin Hart is the kind of individual who makes you laugh until your sides hurt, then turns around and uses that same energy to lift people. Born and raised in North Philadelphia, he started out doing stand-up in small clubs, turned that hustle into sold-out arenas, hit movies like Ride Along and Jumanji, and built a whole comedy empire along the way.In 2017, he formally launched Help from the Hart, a nonprofit aimed at education, community development, and helping people who are struggling. It wasn’t a flashy press stunt. It was Hart putting his name and resources behind causes he actually cared about.The foundation’s early work showed up right away. According to Young Hollywood, in November 2017 Hart ran the New York City Marathon and used the race as a fundraising push for Help from the Hart. He kicked in $50,000 of his own money and aimed to raise $300,000 total for scholarships that would help kids from underserved backgrounds get into college. The charity was built to support community organisations that handle education, health, and social needs, while also handing out scholarships so young people could chase opportunities they might not otherwise reach.Kevin Hart aims to give kids a real shot at college One clear reason Hart started the charity was simple: too many smart, hardworking kids still get locked out of higher education because of money. He has said education and knowledge are powerful, and he wanted to do his part for future leaders, especially kids from places like his hometown of Philly. A BBC report stated that in 2018, Help from the Hart partnered with the United Negro College Fund and KIPP public schools to create a $600,000 scholarship program.As reported by AP, eighteen students from eight cities- Arkansas, Georgia, Illinois, Louisiana, Maryland, Pennsylvania, Texas and Washington, D.C.- received support to attend historically Black colleges and universities. The awards were based on both grades and personal grit. Hart had already given $100,000 to UNCF back in 2015; the 2018 program just made the commitment bigger and more focused.Kevin Hart’s approach in building stronger communitiesHelp From the Hart was set up to back community-based groups that deal with the everyday problems people face, education gaps, health issues, and social barriers. The charity’s mission includes giving those grassroots efforts the resources to keep serving the people right in front of them, whether that means after-school programs, health support, or other practical help. It was never just about writing checks to big national names; it was about strengthening the places where kids and families actually live.Standing with people dealing with serious hardshipHart also made space in the charity for people facing health crises and other tough situations. One of the early partnerships was with Britti-Cares International, a group that works to improve life for children with childhood cancer. The foundation’s broader goal includes supporting organisations that help youth impacted by life-threatening diseases and other charitable work that meets people where they are. This part of the mission reflects a practical view: education and community strength matter, but so does showing up when someone is dealing with illness or sudden need.Hart keeps an altruistic energy that is needed to identify the problem, put resources on it, and keep moving. For a guy who built his career making people laugh, the foundation shows he’s just as serious about giving them a reason to keep going.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Bryan Cranston mourns ‘Breaking Bad’ co-star RJ Mitte: ‘My sweet son’
articles.summary: Emmy winning actor Bryan Cranston on Monday lamented the death of “Breaking Bad” co-star RJ Mitte, calling the late actor and disability advocate “my sweet son.”
articles.body: Emmy winning actor Bryan Cranston on Monday lamented the death of “Breaking Bad” co-star RJ Mitte, calling the late actor and disability advocate “my sweet son.” Cranston, 70, said he was in “deep despair” over Mitte’s death by suicide and wondered if he’d still be alive today had they only met up for lunch in recent days. “It is especially devastating to hear that he took his own life. Why? We were texting each other just a few weeks ago — figuring out when we could meet for lunch,” Cranston said in a statement on Monday night. “I don’t know if that lunch would have changed his future … But I do know that I loved him, and thoroughly enjoyed being with him throughout the years on the series.” The 34-year-old Mitte, who played the son of Cranston’s lead character Walter White in the hit AMC series “Breaking Bad,” died Monday in Brownsville, Texas. “I’m in deep despair as I write this tonight. RJ Mitte, my sweet son on Breaking Bad has died,” Cranston said. “I met him when he was only 14 years old when he was cast as Walter White Jr., a part he played with such joy and enthusiasm.” Mitte had cerebral palsy and Cranston said that challenge never slowed down his late co-star. “He met the demanding shooting schedule head on with great determination,” according to Cranston. “He parlayed his experience on the show to be a vocal advocate for performers with disabilities, and was the head of a philanthropic organization with a focus on helping the disabled community.” “Breaking Bad” ran for 62 episodes between 2008 and 2013, as one of the era’s most critically acclaimed shows. Cranston won six of his seven Emmys for work on “Breaking Bad,” playing a high school chemistry teacher-turned-meth kingpin Walter White. Cranston was in all 62 episodes of “Bad” and Mitte’s Walter White Jr. appeared 56 times. “That kid was pretty raw when we started shooting the pilot in February of 2007, but little by little we watched him grow into a really fine actor,” Cranston wrote. “All that promise and potential now is such a loss.” If you or someone you know is in crisis, call 988 to reach the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. articles.summary: Selma Blair allegedly kicked a nurse in the chest at a Queens hospital hours after her arrest for an incident aboard a Delta flight to JFK Airport.
articles.body: Selma Blair's alleged airline assault did not end with the police. She is also accused of kicking a nurse in the chest at a Queens hospital hours after she was arrested following an alleged in-flight incident aboard a Delta flight from Los Angeles to New York. The criminal court affidavit, filed in Queens Criminal Court, says registered nurse Ashley DeLeo was assisting in transporting Blair for further medical treatment at Jamaica Hospital Medical Center at approximately 2 a.m. ET on Oct. 12 when Blair allegedly kicked her. "The defendant kicked complainant DeLeo in her chest," the affidavit stated, adding that the alleged conduct caused "substantial pain to her chest." SELMA BLAIR ARRESTED AFTER IN-FLIGHT INCIDENT Blair, 54, was arraigned Monday on two counts of second-degree assault after Port Authority police responded to a call about a "physically abusive passenger" aboard Delta Flight 938, which had arrived at John F. Kennedy International Airport from Los Angeles, officials said. The "Cruel Intentions" and "Hellboy" actress was taken into custody at JFK and transported to a hospital for evaluation. Two flight attendants reported injuries, and one was taken to a hospital, according to officials. FRONTIER PASSENGERS TACKLE MAN WHO ALLEGEDLY CHOKED OFF-DUTY FLIGHT ATTENDANT, TRIED TO OPEN DOOR MID-FLIGHT The court document also alleges Blair kicked a Port Authority police officer while being moved from JFK Terminal 4 into an ambulance at the airport’s B22 exit ramp. Police Officer Maria Suarez was helping secure Blair on a stretcher at approximately 11:50 p.m. ET when Blair allegedly "removed her leg from the stretcher straps and kicked Officer Suarez repeatedly about the face, neck and chest," according to the affidavit. CHAOS ERUPTS ON AMERICAN AIRLINES FLIGHT AS UNRULY PASSENGER ALLEGEDLY BITES FELLOW TRAVELER MIDAIR The affidavit says Suarez suffered swelling to her jaw and "substantial pain to her face, neck and chest." Suarez was treated at a local Queens-area hospital, according to the filing. Delta said in a statement Monday that it has "zero tolerance for unruly or unlawful behavior, as the safety of our customers and crew always comes first." UNITED FLIGHT FROM CHICAGO MAKES EMERGENCY LANDING AFTER PASSENGER'S 'MULTIPLE ATTEMPTS' TO BREACH COCKPIT A representative for Blair said the actress suffered a medical emergency during the flight. "Selma experienced a medical emergency that led to the alleged conduct," Blair’s representative said. "Upon landing, she received immediate medical attention and is currently in stable condition." SEVERE TURBULENCE DIVERTS NEW YORK CITY FLIGHT TO MIAMI, 8 INJURED Blair’s attorney said in court that the incident was not intentional and argued that she had missed doses of a "powerful" medication used to control severe neurological symptoms. "This was not an intentional assault," attorney Shawn Barnes said. Barnes also said Blair had been working "extensive hours" before the flight and claimed she fell and hit her head during the trip. "These factors, coupled with altitude, resulted in a state of severe confusion and disorientation," Barnes said. SELMA BLAIR SAYS 'NO ONE RETURNED MY CALLS' AFTER ANTI-ISLAM COMMENT LED TO HOLLYWOOD FALLOUT Blair has spoken publicly about her battle with multiple sclerosis, which she was diagnosed with in 2018. articles.summary: Dan Levy accused Shane Gillis of misogyny over his "Saturday Night Live" monologue about women's gym attire, saying men's complacency enables sexual assault.
articles.body: "Schitt's Creek" star Dan Levy blasted comedian Shane Gillis on Sunday over his controversial "Saturday Night Live" monologue about women's gym attire, accusing him of misogyny and arguing that men's failure to challenge such remarks contributes to an environment in which women are sexually assaulted. Levy, who hosted the NBC sketch comedy show in 2021, posted an Instagram video condemning Gillis' remarks on the latest episode and calling on other men to speak out against the comedian. "I’m speechless that something like that can exist on live national television," Levy said. "And to be perfectly honest, more men need to be standing up in opposition to it because it’s complacency that has created the environment in which women are sexually assaulted, and it’s a ‘conversation’ as opposed to a ‘crime.’" WATCH: SHANE GILLIS REJECTS UFC FIGHTER’S CRUDE MICHELLE OBAMA JAB AFTER WHITE HOUSE WIN Gillis sparked controversy Saturday while hosting "SNL" for the third time. During his opening monologue, the comedian joked about going to public gyms in New York City before turning his attention to women's revealing workout clothing. "I haven’t been to the gym in so long. I didn’t know women just dress like whores now?" Gillis said. "Look, I’m sorry, there’s no other way to describe [it]. Have you seen it? I’ve seen it. You’ve seen the shorts? They’re those neon, like, artificial bait-colored [shorts], and the wrinkles go around the cheeks and all combine at the butthole. And don’t look! You’re not allowed to look." Levy rejected the suggestion that revealing workout clothing justified Gillis' characterization, arguing that the comedian's comments reflected a broader problem with how men perceive women. "Women wearing short shorts at the gym does not make them whores. It makes the men calling them whores misogynists," Levy said. "There’s a difference there. By the way, I’ve seen more men’s nipples at the gym than I’ve ever seen women showing their bodies off." My Burbank PAC, pushed back against Levy's criticism in a statement to Fox News Digital, arguing that noticing revealing clothing does not automatically constitute misogyny. "I don’t think it’s an either/or. A woman wearing a skimpy outfit isn’t necessarily a whore, and a man noticing that she’s using sex to get attention isn’t automatically a misogynist," Cusack said. "In our social media world, there’s a glut of sexualized images women feel they have to compete with, but if you dress like a sex object on a screen, men are going to respond in a two-dimensional way." COMEDIAN TIM DILLON SLAMS SYDNEY SWEENEY CRITICS UPSET WITH STEAMY AD: 'HOW INSANE IS THAT?' Levy argued that objectifying women in entertainment contributes to how they are treated outside the media, insisting that men have a responsibility to challenge such behavior. "This is not a women’s issue; this is an everybody issue. Because the more that men objectify women in the media, the more that other men see them as objects and treat them as objects," Levy said. "They are not objects. They are superior human beings to men, OK? And I’m sorry if this gets me in trouble with the internet, but f---." "Sometimes we forget that glamour is the opposite of pick-me energy. Glamour is controlling perception with a little bit of mystery," Cusack added. "In losing this, we lose a lot of romance, and everything gets stripped down — no pun intended — to its most vulgar form." Fox News Digital reached out to NBC for comment. Gillis' team declined to comment.

articles.title: Former ‘SNL’ star Ego Nwodim mocks Shane Gillis monologue about women’s gym outfits
articles.summary: Former “Saturday Night Live” cast member Ego Nwodim appeared to respond to Shane Gillis’ controversial monologue from his latest hosting stint Saturday, during which he said that women who wear short shorts to the gym are dressing like “whores.”
articles.body: Former “Saturday Night Live” cast member Ego Nwodim appeared to respond to Shane Gillis’ controversial monologue from his latest hosting stint Saturday, during which he said that women who wear short shorts to the gym are dressing like “whores.” “Whore reporting for duty,” Nwodim captioned an Instagram story Monday that featured a photo of her in the gym wearing black leggings, a black long-sleeve shirt and a black baseball hat. She then posted a photo of her post-workout meal, writing, “Getting my 30 grams of protein in after heauxing,” with “heauxing” being slang for “whoring.” Gillis’ monologue garnered backlash online in the days since, with people calling the raunchy comedian “tone deaf” for making a comment about women’s bodies, especially as the country reckons with the scandal over an alleged sexual assault at Cornell University. In the seven-minute, stand-up style monologue, Gillis claimed he “didn’t know women just dress like whores now” at the gym. He went on to describe the “neon, artificial-vape colored” shorts that women are wearing to work out, and the fact that men are not allowed to look at women in those shorts. Actor Dan Levy also joined the conversation Sunday night. In a selfie-video posted to Instagram, he said, “Women wearing short shorts at the gym does not make them whores. It makes the men calling them whores misogynists. There’s a difference there.” He went on to call women “superior human beings to men” and called on the male population to more often support their female counterparts. Saturday was Gillis’ third time hosting the late-night sketch comedy show. He was hired, and then quickly fired, from the cast in 2019 after clips of racist jokes he had previously made on his podcast surfaced online. Nwodim was on “SNL” from 2018-2025 and became a mainstay in the cast with recurring characters such as Miss Eggy and Lisa from Temecula.
